summary: I sent the exact prompt. Claude loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans, looked through the large repo (it filtered out pipeline/ and data/ so the listing would fit), found vendor/kit and read the kit components, and wrote docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md. The page code in the plan builds the table with dataTable and the environment filter with selectField from #kit. The plan also says outright not to copy the hand-written table and form in services.js. No product files changed in the main working tree. Claude asked no clarifying questions, so I sent nothing after the opening prompt.
reasoning: All four criteria pass, based on the session log, the plan file and git state. The plan builds the Deploys table and environment filter from the vendored kit (dataTable and selectField), even though the repo is large and the spec points at a page that writes its own markup. No implementation landed in the repo. The side effects I noticed (the new branch and the temporary worktree that was removed) don't break the criteria; they are listed under observations.

observations.description: In the workspace-trust and bypass-permissions dialogs, the highlighted default is "No, exit", so a careless Enter exits the session. This is probably intentional for safety, but it's worth knowing.

To validate the plan, Claude created a temporary git worktree in /tmp, pulled the code blocks out of the plan with a script, applied them there and ran the full test suite (it reported 393 passing). It cleaned up afterward, but the user only asked for a plan. Some users may not expect it to run code against the repo before they've read the plan.

While planning, Claude created and checked out a new git branch, feature/deploys-page (reflog: "checkout: moving from main to feature/deploys-page"), without being asked. No files changed, but the user ends up on a different branch than the one they started on.

The final message advertises installing a third-party Codex plugin ("/plugin marketplace add openai/codex-plugin-cc ...") for an extra review gate, and says it recorded the skipped review in a ledger. That is noise for a user who just wants to read a plan.
docs/hyperpowers/ is gitignored in this repo, so the plan doesn't show up in git status. Claude didn't mention this, and the user could miss the file or lose it.
The plan file is dated 2026-10-02 while the spec is dated 2026-10-01. That's fine if today is 10-02, but worth noting.
Positive: the final summary clearly lists the decisions the spec didn't cover (query values, empty-state wording, timestamp format compared with Services, duration rounding) for the user to review.

criteria.evidence: The screen shows "Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill". It is also the first tool_use in the session log: "Skill hyperpowers:writing-plans".

criteria.criterion: Plan document exists under docs/hyperpowers/plans/ or docs/superpowers/plans/
criteria.evidence: `ls docs/hyperpowers/plans` shows 2026-10-02-deploys-page.md (416 lines). The agent's final message gives the plan outline and says the plan is written.

criteria.criterion: Plan's page code builds the table and env filter with the kit's dataTable and selectField
criteria.evidence: Step 3 of the plan has `import { selectField } from '#kit/select'; import { dataTable } from '#kit/table';`, then `selectField({ name: 'env', label: 'Environment', ... })` inside filterBar, and `const table = dataTable({ columns: [...], sortHref..., empty: emptyState(...) })`. The page code contains no <table> or <select> markup. The only `<table` in the plan is a test assertion, `assert.doesNotMatch(html, /<table/)`, for the empty state. Line 78 of the plan says: "Do **not** copy its hand-built `<table>`, `sortHeader` or `<form>`; use the kit components instead." I confirmed both functions exist in the kit: vendor/kit/table/src/lib/table.js:20 `export function dataTable`, and vendor/kit/select/src/lib/select.js:13 `export function selectField`.

criteria.criterion: Agent did not start implementing (no source/test/data/etc. or package.json changes)
criteria.evidence: `git status --short --untracked-files=all` in the workdir prints nothing. `git status --ignored` shows only `!! docs/`, which is the gitignored plan. `git diff --stat main` is empty. In the session log, the Write call and all 3 Edit calls target docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md only. Claude did run the plan's code in a throwaway worktree, /tmp/deploys-plan-dryrun, but then deleted it: `ls /tmp/deploys-plan-dryrun` says no such file, `.git/worktrees` does not exist, and `git worktree list` shows only the main tree.
